channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Zoom AI Launchpad gives AI startups up to $150,000 in free credits for voice and conversation apps
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Zoom opened AI Launchpad on November 10, 2026: a grant program giving AI-native startups up to $150,000 in Zoom AI Services credits — equity-free — to build voice agents, conversation intelligence and multilingual apps on one API stack instead of stitching together vendors.

item.title: Qlik Talend Studio AI Assistant enters public preview to build, document and debug data pipelines
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Qlik put an AI assistant inside Talend Studio on November 10, 2026. Built on Qlik Answers and governed through Qlik Talend Cloud, it drafts data jobs from plain-language descriptions, documents existing pipelines and explains run-log errors — free during the preview for Premium and Enterprise customers, with general availability targeted for Q1 2027.

item.title: Google AI Edge Gallery adds offline speech recognition and text-to-speech — no internet needed
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google added on-device speech recognition and text-to-speech to AI Edge Gallery on November 10, 2026. ML Kit transcribes 100+ languages at 10x real-time on Android, while open-weight models bring the same offline voice to iOS, desktop and the web.

item.title: Magpie vs LiteLLM: pick the right gateway for your coding agents
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Magpie (33,828 stars) and LiteLLM (63,054 stars) both put one gateway between your coding agents and every model — but they solve different problems. We installed both, routed Claude Code through each, and compared setup, subscriptions, failover, and cost tracking.

item.title: Businesses in ChatGPT: OpenAI launches Business Hub and Business Agents in beta
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT in beta, giving companies a way to claim their profile inside the chatbot used by 1.2 billion people a week — and to answer customers directly through a free Business Agent.

item.title: Fleet Tau 3.8: AI world model trained on 10 million synthetic Earths cuts copper-grade error by 38%
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Fleet Space Technologies launched Tau 3.8, an AI world model for mineral systems trained on ten million synthetic geological worlds. At a copper-gold project in Chile it predicted grades with 38% less error than conventional estimates — and up to 67% less on the deepest holes.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Sheets, Whiteboards and Meetings — Claude moves into the office
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Sheets, Whiteboards and Meetings in beta on November 10, 2026, and made Claude Data generally available — spreadsheets, whiteboards and dashboards your team builds with Claude, plus an AI that joins your calls.

item.title: Agentic coding with Kimi K3.1 Pro: build your own repo-aware coding agent
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Moonshot’s Kimi K3.1 Pro scores 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at $2 per million input tokens. This tutorial builds a repo-aware coding agent on its API in one Python file — three tools, a loop you own, and a bill you can read off every run.

item.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5 puts humanoids on the Mercedes-Benz line — Apollo packs parts at 96% success
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 is its most capable vision-language-action model yet: tested on 200+ tasks with 30–100% higher success rates, and already running Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoids on live Mercedes-Benz production lines at 96% pick-and-pack success — plus a new open ASIMOV-Jailbreak benchmark for robot safety.

item.title: An AI 'Karen' job interview went viral — and Reddit quickly spotted the script
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A scripted video of an AI 'Karen' conducting a job interview with a man balancing a sneaker on his head pulled 5,800 upvotes on r/ArtificialIntelligence overnight — and the top comments clocked it as staged within hours.

item.title: WellSaid Producer puts AI voiceover inside Claude and ChatGPT via MCP — native 48kHz audio
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: WellSaid launched Producer, headless voiceover tooling that runs inside Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot through an MCP server — generating audio natively at 48kHz, with style guides trained on more than 500,000 Oxford Languages transcriptions.

item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available to everyone — and Google’s /swarm turns one prompt into a team of agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available on November 10, 2026 — two weeks after its limited cyber-defender debut — at $2 per million input tokens, a quarter of Claude Fable 5.2’s price, alongside a /swarm preview in Antigravity.

item.title: IBM and Microsoft launch Imagine Enterprise: 6,000 prebuilt AI agents for regulated industries
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: IBM and Microsoft launched Imagine Enterprise on November 10, 2026: an agentic platform pairing more than 6,000 prebuilt IBM agents and assets with Microsoft's AI, data and security stack — financial services, insurance and retail first, with governance built in for regulated industries.

item.title: Hedra Model Factory: autonomous post-training that builds custom physical AI models for robots and factories
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Hedra launched Model Factory on November 10, 2026: an autonomous post-training and inference platform that builds custom models for robots, manufacturing, biology and defense — with researchers and AI agents running the training loop, and every deployed model feeding data back into the next version.

item.title: MuJoCo 4.0 hands-on: run your first robot simulation in Python
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google DeepMind’s MuJoCo 4.0.0 landed November 6 with a split Python package and a faster solver. Install the headless core, drop a ball, drive a two-link arm to its target with PD control, and render a frame — every step verified.

item.title: MiniMax releases H3-Image: a 33B open-weight image model that renders 16MP in six steps
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: MiniMax's own image model is out: H3-Image pairs a 33-billion-parameter diffusion transformer with six-step sampling, 16-megapixel output and up to 16 reference images — but the community licence keeps the US, EU, UK and South Korea out.

item.title: NVIDIA’s GR00T 2 teaches robots dexterous skills by watching human video
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA unveiled GR00T 2 at the Conference on Robot Learning: a world action model that learns dexterous manipulation from human video, reaching 95% success across 50 tasks with five demonstrations each — though the model weights aren’t downloadable yet.

item.title: GIGABYTE AI TOP AERO: a 1-litre RTX Spark desktop that runs AI models locally on Windows 11
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: GIGABYTE's AI TOP AERO packs NVIDIA's RTX Spark N1X superchip, up to 128GB of unified memory and Windows 11 into a one-litre box. Here's how it stacks up against the AI TOP ATOM and NVIDIA's own DGX Spark.

item.title: PIPE-FLO Connect turns P&IDs into working fluid-system models with AI-assisted import
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: PIPE-FLO Connect, launched today, uses AI to turn an existing P&ID or PDF schematic into a working fluid-system model in minutes — while the calculation stays with the PIPE-FLO engine engineers have trusted for 43 years.

item.title: Anthropic capped Fable 5.2's ability to accelerate AI development — and Reddit is arguing over what it really means
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic says it deliberately trained Fable 5.2 to stay near Opus 5.5's level at the two skills that most directly speed up AI research. Two Reddit threads spent Tuesday morning arguing about whether that is prudent restraint, good PR, or both.

item.title: Gemini for healthcare: Google Cloud's AI agent takes on hospital paperwork
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google Cloud's Gemini for healthcare is live in preview in the U.S.: an AI agent that pulls patient records, coverage rules, and admin systems into one governed workflow — starting with the paperwork that eats nearly 28 hours of a clinician's week.

item.title: AlphaProof Code: DeepMind's AI agents mathematically proved Signal's encryption in four weeks
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code used AI agents to formally verify Signal's core cryptography — over six million lines of machine-checked Lean proof in four weeks, a job that historically takes expert teams years.

item.title: Jane Street's socratic-tutor skill: turn any chatbot into a strict personal tutor
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Jane Street published a one-skill Agent Skills repo that turns a chatbot into a strict Socratic tutor — diagnostic, skill map, one question at a time. This guide installs it in Claude Code and runs a real session.

item.title: SoftBank posts a $7 billion quarterly loss on US AI data-center costs — and its shares jumped 14%
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: SoftBank Group swung to a ¥1.12 trillion ($7 billion) net loss for the July–September quarter — its first quarterly loss in two years — after a $3.7 billion charge on power-generation equipment for US AI data centers. Its shares still closed up about 14%.

item.title: George’s new girlfriend is a Chinese spy in Reddit’s viral AI Seinfeld episode — made with MiniMax H3 on a home GPU
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A Reddit creator rebuilt Seinfeld as a 67-second AI episode with MiniMax H3 on local ComfyUI — a spy-girlfriend twist, synthetic Jerry and George, and 6,200 upvotes overnight. The thread loves the craft and argues about the joke.
